claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances and any children you're responsible for.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you currently have any children under 16 years old, or children aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - Alex, who's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know that Alex is 8 years old.

Now, to continue assessing your eligibility:

**Do you live in the UK, and do you live with Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I live in the UK, but Alex doesn't live with me - he lives with his mum.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. So Alex lives with his mum, but you're still involved in his life.

**Are you currently making financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep, such as paying for his food, clothes, pocket money, or other living expenses?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not currently able to contribute financially at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being clear about that.

Just to confirm the full picture:

**Has Alex been living with his mum for more than 8 weeks now, or is this a recent arrangement?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's been living with his mum for quite a while now - definitely more than 8 weeks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the information you've shared:

- Alex is 8 years old and lives with his mum
- You don't live with Alex
- You're not currently making financial contributions towards his upkeep
- Alex has been living with his mum for more than 8 weeks

According to Child Benefit rules, you can normally continue to receive Child Benefit for 8 weeks after a child goes to live with someone else. However, you can continue receiving payments beyond 8 weeks only if you're making financial contributions to the child's upkeep that are at least equal to the Child Benefit payment amount.

Since Alex has been with his mum for more than 8 weeks and you're not currently contributing financially towards his upkeep, you would not be eligible to receive Child Benefit for Alex at this time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that based on your circumstances, **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

The key issue is that while Child Benefit can continue for 8 weeks after a child moves to live with someone else, that period has now passed in your case. To be eligible beyond those 8 weeks, you would need to be making regular financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep that are at least equal to the Child Benefit payment amount. Since you're not currently able to do this, you don't meet the eligibility criteria.

However, if your financial situation changes in the future and you become able to contribute towards Alex's upkeep, you could contact HMRC to discuss whether you might become eligible again.
